title: Dragapult
gamePlan: Evolve into Dragapult ex and use Phantom Dive to combine Active damage with six damage counters on the Bench. Drakloak supports the evolution setup.
strengths: Pressures several targets with one attack.
Damage-counter placement creates flexible Prize routes.
weaknesses: A Stage 2 attacker requires a prepared evolution line.
Needs both Fire and Psychic Energy for Phantom Dive.
suggestions: Balance Dreepy, Drakloak and Dragapult with evolution/search support.
Plan Bench counters around future knockouts rather than isolated damage.

title: Basic Box
gamePlan: Use a selection of Basic attackers for different board states. Mega Kangaskhan ex supplies Active-position draw, while Teal Mask Ogerpon ex supports a Grass Energy engine.
strengths: Basic attackers reduce evolution setup requirements.
Several attackers allow different tactical routes.
weaknesses: Multiple Energy requirements compete for deck space.
Rule Box attackers expose multiple Prizes when knocked out.
suggestions: Keep Energy access aligned with the attackers you actually plan to use.
Review opening Pokémon and switching options alongside the draw engine.

title: Slowking
gamePlan: Seek Inspiration copies an attack from a discarded non-Rule-Box Pokémon on top of the deck. Build around controlling that top card and matching copied attacks to the situation.
strengths: A single-Prize main attacker can support flexible exchanges.
weaknesses: An unsuitable top card can make the attack fail.
Requires both evolution setup and reliable top-deck control.
suggestions: Check each chosen attack donor against Seek Inspiration restrictions.
Include a plan for recovering discarded attackers and resetting the deck top.

title: Alakazam Dudunsparce
gamePlan: Grow the hand with Psychic Draw and Run Away Draw, then use Powerful Hand to place damage counters according to hand size.
strengths: Powerful Hand scales with cards held in hand.
weaknesses: Hand disruption reduces the attack ceiling.
Several evolution lines can compete for setup resources.
suggestions: Preserve hand resources before committing to Powerful Hand.
Balance the Alakazam and Dudunsparce lines with recovery and search.

title: Dragapult Dusknoir
gamePlan: Combine Phantom Dive spread with Dusknoir’s Cursed Blast to reach knockout thresholds. Cursed Blast also knocks out your own Dusknoir, so map both sides of the Prize exchange.
strengths: Additional targeted damage counters can finish difficult targets.
Several simultaneous knockout routes can emerge.
weaknesses: Cursed Blast gives up a Pokémon and potentially a Prize.
A second Stage 2 line increases setup demands.
suggestions: Count Prizes before using Cursed Blast.
Preserve enough resources to rebuild the main attacker after a knockout.

title: Dragapult Blaziken
gamePlan: Use Blaziken ex’s Seething Spirit to recover Basic Energy from the discard and support Dragapult’s multi-type attack cost.
strengths: Recurring Energy attachment supports rebuilding attackers.
Blaziken can serve as an alternate attacking route.
weaknesses: Two Stage 2 lines need space and setup time.
Energy recovery depends on Energy reaching the discard.
suggestions: Map the evolution counts for both lines.
Keep Basic Energy and discard access consistent with Seething Spirit.

title: Dragapult Dudunsparce
gamePlan: Support Dragapult’s spread plan with Run Away Draw. Recycling Dudunsparce changes Bench space and requires rebuilding its line on later turns.
strengths: A renewable draw option supports the Stage 2 setup.
Returning Dudunsparce can free Bench space.
weaknesses: Both lines need repeated evolution access.
Draw does not by itself guarantee the right Energy mix.
suggestions: Check the Dunsparce count against repeated Run Away Draw uses.
Keep a separate plan for finding Fire and Psychic Energy.

title: Hydrapple
gamePlan: Attach Grass Energy through Ripening Charge and the Ogerpon engine, then scale Syrup Storm with Energy across your board.
strengths: Ripening Charge also heals the receiving Pokémon.
weaknesses: A large Energy board is a resource commitment.
Hydrapple is a Stage 2 attacker requiring evolution access.
suggestions: Balance Basic Grass Energy with reliable search/recovery.
Consider how to rebuild Energy attachments after a knockout.

title: N's Zoroark
gamePlan: Use Trade to cycle the hand and Night Joker to copy attacks from Benched N’s Pokémon.
strengths: Night Joker offers several attacks through the Bench.
weaknesses: Attack choices depend on specific Benched Pokémon.
Trade costs a discard that may remove future resources.
suggestions: Review Bench space, Darkness Energy access and recovery together.
